utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, The Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Today, we are going to continue the cross-examination by Mr. Karnavas. I hope that we could finish the cross-examination today. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Karnavas: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On Friday we left off when I had handed you what had been previously marked as Defence Exhibit, for identification purpose, D21/1. I take it you didn't have an opportunity to look it over during the weekend.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not have an opportunity of looking it over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. If you could be so kind as to give it a quick look, and then I would like to go over it with you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I would like to correct the record. It's Exhibit D22/1 I think you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right, D22.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And not 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You're absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have taken a look at it, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nikolic. This document which has an identification number at the top of it as DA01-0961 was provided to us by the Office of the Prosecution. Do you know whether your lawyers had an opportunity to share this document with you which obviously they had received as part of their disclosure material?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I did not have an opportunity of acquainting myself with this document up until the present time. That means I didn't have it among the documents given to me by my lawyers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. If we could just go through parts of the document initially to lay a little bit of a foundation, at the top of the page, it indicates a date of October 24, 1994, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it indicates that it comes from the headquarters of the Republika Srpska Army, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one can see that from the heading.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And if we were -- and it's titled -- it's titled "Instruction on Management and Command of Security Intelligence Agencies of Republika Srpska (RSA)," or in Srpski, it would be VRS. Does it not say that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you would be so kind as to flip over to the last page - I believe it's a three-page document - at the bottom of the page, it has a signature, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It also has -- the copy is rather poor, but it would seem to indicate that there was a seal along with the signature, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would look like it. I can see the contours, so I suppose that was a stamp, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it appears that the person who signed it was Ratko Mladic. Does it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say is that it says "Commander, Lieutenant-General Ratko Mladic," but I really can't say whether the signature is actually his because I don't know General Mladic's signature so I can't actually confirm that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But right above the signature, it has: "Commander, Lieutenant-General Ratko Mladic," and that's typed in?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And would this not appear to be an official document?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it looks like an official document, because we can see where it comes from and who the signatory is, so that's quite obvious.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, on the last page, the last sentence right above the stamp with the signature and the designation, the last sentence reads, and correct me if I read it wrong: "This order is to be delivered and introduced to all commanders of units, institutions, up to and including battalions." Does it not state that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And a battalion is within a brigade?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so at least it would appear --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, Mr. Karnavas, this could mean something else, another thing. It could refer to the individual infantry battalions, so I'm not quite sure that this refers to battalions within the brigade, but independent infantry battalions. But it is possible, so I don't exclude that possibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think rather it refers to independent infantry battalions rather than otherwise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But from reading this last sentence, would it not appear to be a logical conclusion that this document would have gone to a brigade such as the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is logical.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we could go through this document step by step, and I'm going to please focus your attention - we won't spend much time on the first part, the first paragraph - but I would like you to focus your attention on the parts where it says "instruction," and then they are enumerated. On number 2, it reads, and if you could follow along with me: "A person in direct command of a security intelligence agency is the commander of the unit institution within which the agency operates." Does it not state that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from that sentence, does it not -- would we not conclude that the commander they're talking about, in your instance, would have been your commander, Colonel Blagojevic? Just the first sentence.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this instruction, we can see a general principle discussed, "commanders." Now, if you ask me in this particular case who my brigade commander was, then of course it was Colonel Blagojevic, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly. And that's precisely what I asked you, whether your commander was Colonel Blagojevic and whether this sentence applies to him. Right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It applies to all the unit commanders and commanders of institutions, which includes him, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to Momir Nikolic, that's who we're talking about, with respect to Momir Nikolic, this paragraph, this sentence refers to your commander, Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let's read on. "But with regard to professional activities, they are under the centralised management of the security intelligent agencies of the superior command. This emphasises their full independence in accomplishment of intelligence and counterintelligence tasks as well as in operational combining on the grounds of the authority vested in them by law and the authority given by the competent superior branch agencies regarding the implementation of methods and means used in operation, in accordance with law." Does it not state that, Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does state that, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would it not be a fair, accurate, and complete interpretation of what I just read to you that when it comes to professional activities, you would be fully independent, does it not state that, this part right here that I just read?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. However, only within the framework of what it says here. That means that it indicates their full independence in accomplishment of intelligence and counterintelligence tasks as well as in operational combining on the grounds of the authority vested in them by law and the authority given by the competent agencies regarding the implementation of methods. Just in that respect and in that portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't want the witness eating the clock. I just read the section to him, he's reading it back on the record. There is no need for the witness if he wishes to give a qualification as to what I just read I have no objection. For the witness to be reading as he did on Friday in order to eat up the time, I object to that. He is intelligent, he's read it, he can give his interpretation. That's all I'm asking, Your Honour. I'm not asking him to reread it to us. We are not stupid in the courtroom. We have read it; we understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I think you have to be patient to let the witness give an explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree with you, Your Honour. I will be eminently patient for an explanation, but I dare say that I will lose my patience if he's just going to be reading what I just already read. It doesn't get us anywhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think you know this instruction is also explanation there. Maybe the witness could offer us more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would hope so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, at the outset, I stated that this document was not one that I had an opportunity to read through and have --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour, to the speech making.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think this issue is relevant because at first, you pointed out this document is distributed to all the commanders of the units, institutions, up and including the battalions. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, which means --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But this witness told us that he has never seen this document before. There must be a reason for that. I think the witness is also a commander of a unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: There's a point in it. You have to be patient.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I will be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Nikolic, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as I was saying, I wish to repeat what I tried to say a moment ago. As I said, I did not see this document before. I did not have it as part of the documents disclosed to me by the OTP and my lawyers in the Detention Unit. That's the first point. Secondly, Mr. Karnavas, from this document, I -- and let me say I received hundreds of documents, instructions, and orders, and so on. All I can do here now is to testify to this Trial Chamber as to whether I had it, whether I used it only if on this document it were to say who this document was addressed to and sent to. From this, we cannot see, Mr. Karnavas, that this particular document, this set of instructions, went to the commander in person. I can't see that stated anywhere. And my next point, I cannot see that this document was sent to the security intelligence organ in person. I cannot see from this document either that it states that the security intelligence organ was informed of it. So after seven or eight years, all I can do is to analyse the document if it says that it was addressed to the commander and then to the Bratunac Brigade, the Zvornik Brigade, and so on, other brigades as well, and it expressly states that this document was addressed to the security intelligence organ of the Bratunac Brigade. It is only at that point that I would be able to say whether I actually had the document and was given it. But to the best of my recollections, I can just say whether I know about a document, whether it's familiar to me or not. But I can't actually confirm whether I had it in my possession, and I claim that in the Detention Unit I never had this document in my possession and I did not have an opportunity to read it. That is why, and you're asking me some very specific and concrete details, I have to read through it. I really do have to read every sentence carefully in order to be able to respond to your questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Nikolic. Let's read on, and then after we go through the various paragraphs, I won't ask you to interpret; I will just ask you at the end one question, and that is: Were you aware what the policy that's contained in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The witness has not had a chance to answer the original question he was interrupted in answering. He probably doesn't remember it any more. I'm not sure I do. But he was reading back a sentence and was going to offer an explanation to it. And he was interrupted and has not been given a chance to answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, will you repeat your first question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 2, from the document that the OTP gave us, gave to your counsel, it says here that with respect to professional activities, you would have full independence, and that aspect of it is emphasised, is it not, in this paragraph? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is emphasised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, later on, the last paragraph, it states: "Besides all members of such agencies and services have lawful authority to proceed on tasks within their scope of work, and those correspond to the authorities of members of the RS ministry of internal affairs, state security department;" does it not state that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, you've confused me again. We were talking about paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 2, at the end of the -- paragraph number 2, at the very end, the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it now. I've read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, paragraph 3, the first part: "It is an obligation of all RSA units and institution commands as well as the obligation of other army members to render any assistance to these agencies required to accomplish their tasks without jeopardising through a single act the security and protection of planned intelligence and counterintelligence tasks and actions undertaken locally as well as in an enemy territory." Does it not state that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we conclude from reading that that the intelligence organ and the security organ institutions that this document is referring to should get the full cooperation and assistance from their commanders? If you don't understand the question, just tell me.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, what it says here is that it is the obligation of all commands and units. It doesn't say "all commanders"; it says "all commands." And that is the distinction that I have to make, and it is not quite identical to what you said. "As well as other members of the army," you did say that, so I can confirm that. So it is the obligation of all commands and units, and I can explain what this specifically means, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it says -- it begins by saying "it is an obligation..." In other words, can we assume or conclude that they don't have a choice, it's not an option; it is an obligation? They must.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, all these obligations are defined by the rules of service in the armed forces. And there's nothing new here, absolutely nothing new. What we are reading now is defined in the rules of service regarding the work of the security organs and the rules of service regarding security and intelligence. So there's nothing new that this instruction defines that is not already covered by the rules of service. I know --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Nikolic, did I ask you whether there was anything new --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's the third time this morning. I know he doesn't want to hear from this witness, but...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's absolutely incorrect. The question was quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's a little early for this kind of argumentativeness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsels please not speak at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm not allowing that the counsels argue with each other in front of a Judge. If there's any problem, just refer to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I asked a specific question. I was directed on Friday by the Trial Bench to ask specific concrete questions. I asked a specific concrete question. I'm getting a historical analysis of what the rules are. That's not what I asked. I didn't ask whether there was something new in this. I asked whether the word "obligations" means that they are obliged. Now, either the gentleman understands the question and he can answer it, or he cannot understand it and I wish to remind the Trial Chamber that this Prosecutor here entered into an agreement with him and his lawyers, and he agreed that he was going to testify truthfully and honestly and completely and forthrightly. And that means not trying to evade and dodge the questions, Your Honour. That's all I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think that the witness is going to help us as much as possible. And when you ask a question, you should allow the witness to give you a very concise explanation why he did that. Mr. Nikolic, try to make your answer as concise as possible because this is a question/answer proceeding, and you have to be directed or led by the counsel. Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it goes on in the same paragraph: "Simultaneously, it is a duty of the members of the security intelligent agency to directly inform the superior commanders, to a necessary extent, on the data, assessments, and observations, related to security of units institutions." Mr. Nikolic, is that what the statement -- is that what is stated in this document?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to go to paragraph 4. Second part of the paragraph reads: "All wires and mail of the security intelligence command members are to be hand-delivered, these persons only and no other authority of command, including the commander, has the right of inspection of the contents. The method and the extent to which the content of these telegrams or mail will be introduced to a command or another commanding body will be regulated only, and no one but the competent security intelligence agencies." Does it not state that, Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to paragraph 5, now, this paragraph is sectioned off, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm going to object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas has a duty in the Rule to put his point to the witness. If he has a point in regarding paragraph 5, he has a duty under these rules to ask him about it, not just have him parrot back what the rules say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: There are two ways to do it. One is paragraph by paragraph. The other -- maybe after all those confirmations of what is written in this document, Mr. Karnavas will drive his nail.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I hope so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's exactly what I'm going to be doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Okay. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 5, it says: "Personal policies and in-service management of members of these agencies is under the exclusive authority of the commander of RSA or VRS command and assistant commander of RSA command for security intelligence. In relation to this, security intelligence sector of RSA command decides on the security intelligence agencies members' transfers, assignments, and special tasks within their scope of activities." Does it not state that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it states, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then the next part says: "Commander of units and institutions of RSA whose subordinates include members of the aforementioned agency may be consulted on these issues and give suggestions, but will make no decisions on them." Does it not state that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next point: "Commanders of units and institutions may impose stimulating penalties and other measures against members of such agencies upon compulsory consultation with the first in command in the service." It states that, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from this, would it appear that if your commander, Colonel Blagojevic, wished to punish you, he would have to make the request through Popovic or Beara? Does it not state that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one could interpret that in that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And on number 7, if we go to number 7, it says: "Control of expertise, legality, and propriety of work of security intelligence agencies shall only be performed by the first in command of the security intelligence affairs agency, except in the part of their work that relates to the command/headquarters affairs." Does it not state that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the latter part of paragraph 7 where it says "except in the part of their work that relates to command or headquarters affairs," does that not relate in general, in essence, to office work, paperwork?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Would it be fair to assume or conclude that the first part of paragraph 7 in essence states that it is Popovic and Beara that assess your expertise and performance in the event you are up for a promotion? Assess your expertise and performance; not recommend, but make the assessment.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way that you have put it is not right. With regard to promotions, that is not so. It says here clearly: "Control of expertise." This has to do within the tasks and duties within the scope of work of the security organ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just digress here for a second. You were a captain, were you not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You weren't even a first-class captain, you were just a captain. Right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were not a major?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, I was not a major? What do you mean? If I'm a captain, then of course I'm not a major.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you would on various occasions represent yourself to be a major. That was part of your repertoire, was it not, when you were a liaison with the DutchBat?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can explain that to Their Honours, if you're asking me why I represented myself as a major.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First I would like to know whether you did. That was the question. Did you not, in fact, Momir Nikolic, chief of intelligence and security, represent yourself as a major, sometimes even higher, like a chief of staff, maybe even a general? Did you not do that, in fact, sir, when you were -- back then in 1995 and before?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Again, that is another three-or four part question. Some of it assumes facts that are not in evidence. He has a duty when he asks these questions that there be some basis in fact. I don't recall anyone ever saying that Momir Nikolic represented himself as a general.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He can answer the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, first, break your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Then using the simplest language to express your view --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- Don't make all of us get confused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you not represent yourself to be a major? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, in contacts with representatives of the Dutch Battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever represent yourself or lead them to believe that you were the chief of staff of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never did I lead them to believe regarding any of my duties. Simply, I never told them the real truth about what I was doing, and I worked as an intelligence officer. And that is quite normal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. You lied?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't lie. It is one of the ways of protecting myself, my functional duties, et cetera. It is one of the measures, customary measures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We're going to get into that. But let's get back to this, and we'll get into that area. Now, on paragraph 8, the last paragraph, we're back to this document here that has been marked for identification purposes as D21/1 -- D22/1, sorry, Mr. Registrar. Paragraph number 8 says: "Commanders and other superior officers at all levels who manage security intelligence agencies shall strictly abide by this order." Does it not state that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, that is what it states.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, having -- now that we have gone through this document, one general question: Were you familiar with the policies that are set in this document when you were operating as a security and intelligence -- the chief of security and intelligence of the Bratunac Brigade around July of 1995? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection to the form of the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This insistence on yes or no questions has been dealt with by the Court. That is not a proper question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's not a yes or no question. Of course Mr. Karnavas will allow the witness to give an explanation because it's a complicated matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have been giving the witness opportunities to explain. First, if he could say yes or no. If he says no, then I will ask him how is it possible? If he says, maybe we'll have a discussion on that point. But first we need to get to whether he knows the policies in here. We know he hasn't read it. We know he hasn't seen it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I think there's maybe a cultural difference. In some cultures, it's very difficult to answer a question beginning with yes or no. But anyway, we will hear what the witness is going to tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have already partly tried to answer this question. As regards this document, I have already said that I did not have occasion to have it at my disposal here and that while I held this position in the command of the Bratunac Brigade, there were many documents, orders, and instructions directed towards the organ of which I was the chief. On the basis of this -- these instructions that I now have in front of me, I cannot assert that I received them. Regards all these duties and obligations, I remember how they are defined in the rules of service, which I used. So I can say that this regulation of matters is nothing new for me. I was familiar with my obligations and duties and other matters defined by these instructions even before these instructions arrived. I would state that on the first page, it says that these instructions were forwarded to the commander and for the information of the intelligence and security organs. And if that was so, I should have received it, and I would know of it. So that would briefly be my explanation with regard to this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One follow-up question, Mr. Nikolic, because I want to make sure that I understand and everyone else here understands the answer that you just gave. Though you did not see this document that was signed by General Mladic and directed at least in part to your sector, it is your position today that everything that's contained in this particular document you already knew and was in compliance of or applied while you were a member of the chief of intelligence and security of the Bratunac Brigade back in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, again, you have stated something that I did not say, that it was partially addressed to my service. I have already answered that question, that it was addressed to the intelligence and security organ. I would know that if it said so on this document, that it was sent to the heads of intelligence and security organs of the brigade. In that case, I would tell you with certainty it was sent to my brigade, to me in person, and I received it. As it is, neither you nor I can see to whom it was addressed, that it was sent to the commander it doesn't say, nor does it say that it was sent to the chief of intelligence and security. So I cannot claim that it arrived and that I had it because I really don't remember. Hundreds of wires and telegrams, demands and instructions reached the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that wasn't my question. My question was whether he understood the policies that are contained in this document. I just wanted that answer. He has already indicated to us that he didn't receive it. I accept that answer, that he didn't see it. All I want to know specifically what's contained in this document, the policy matters, did he know them at the time and if so, did he apply them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I think the witness has already answered your question. The transcript is very clear. He said I was familiar with my obligations and duties and other matters defined by those instruments even before those instructions arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move on to another topic, Mr. Nikolic. From the -- I understand it that before coming here today and before making your agreement with the Prosecution, you spent considerable time, you, your lawyers, and the Prosecutor, negotiating, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, negotiations began sometime in November, did they not? They began last year?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know the exact date. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking for a specific date. I'm asking for a month. Did they not start back early November, say, around November 5? Somewhere around there, first week of November?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat again, I don't remember whether it was November or December the negotiations started. Several months ago, and I really cannot tell you exactly when.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it took approximately six months or so for you, your lawyers, and the Prosecutor to reach an agreement that you found acceptable. Is that not a fact?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It took as long as it did. So we started the negotiations. I didn't keep track of the number of months. We started, we negotiated, and in the end we reached an agreement. And that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we reaching this agreement, at your disposal you had the disclosure material, at least the part that your lawyers shared with you?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Karnavas, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you spent literally hundreds of hours with your lawyers discussing parts of the document that were disclosed to you. Is that not a fact?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With my lawyers, I spent as many hours as they, or rather I and my lawyers thought we needed to prepare ourselves with respect to my defence. Now, how many hours that took, I really didn't add up. Whether it was hundreds, I really don't know. But in any event, we did meet very frequently and regularly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it if we were to go to the Detention Unit and get the records as to when and how often and for how long your lawyers met with you, we would have a better ballpark figure as to the exact amount of hours that you spent with your lawyers discussing your defence, as they should be doing because that's part of their job. Right? The Detention Unit would have those records, would they not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, they probably have those records.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And in the course of discussing the disclosure material with your lawyers, it became fairly obvious what the Prosecution's theory of the case was with respect to Momir Nikolic, did it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to object to the relevancy of going into the client/counsel privilege in preparing for their defence. I don't see how it ties into their plea agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It will tie in, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The client/counsel privilege still exists, and I have no idea of the relevance of that last question. Or the propriety of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I think I have to remind you that the witness gave up many of his rights. But he kept his right to have his counsel represented. So you should respect the privileges between counsel and his client.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If this question is not extremely crucial to your case, I hope you could skip it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll go about it in another way, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point, you began to meet with the Prosecutor, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We don't have a tape-recorded statement of what exactly you and the Prosecutor and your lawyers talked or negotiated or bargained over, do we?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I don't know whether you have that or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Whose choice -- so you don't know, when you were present in the room speaking Mr. McCloskey and his folks, you were not aware that there was not a tape recorder there?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did know that, Mr. Karnavas, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, you knew that there wasn't a tape recorder there because you and your lawyers had insisted that whatever went on in that particular room was between those who are in that particular room at that particular time. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not reach an agreement with respect to that matter. I was invited, that is to say, I was informed that the talks would begin with the Prosecutor in the presence of my lawyers. As to the procedure around all this, what obligations each party had, I really don't know. I can't say. Quite simply, that was procedure that I followed and accepted, and I didn't know whether anything was to be recorded or not at that point in time. So I behaved as I was asked to do. I talked to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say that respect to those matters, those matters were decided by your lawyers and Mr. McCloskey as to whether it should be tape-recorded or not tape-recorded, whether we should have a transparent process or a nontransparent process?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Asking the witness to speculate on matters the witness has already talked about not knowing anything about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, I believe that you could not get more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to skip ahead a little bit, and then we'll come back. The Prosecutor asked you on the last day when he was questioning you about certain -- a certain information report prepared by his investigator, Mr. Bursik. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact, Mr. Bursik went over part of his information report with you, did he not?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, just to clarify the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I know counsel meant to say when I was questioning him at trial, and just so we know that because there was a lot of questioning, and I'm not sure you were here at that point. So I just wanted to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Make some clarification for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You met with the Prosecutor several days - I think it was four or five days - proofing what you had said on previous occasions in preparation for trial. Isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We talked about different subjects relating to the factual basis, and we also discussed other matters, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And one of the matters that was discussed was an information report prepared by Bruce Bursik of the OTP Office. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did discuss that piece of information, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bursik had been in the room while you were discussing or debriefing Mr. McCloskey prior to reaching a plea agreement with him. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Bursik was in the room when we started our conversation, as far as I remember. And after that, for a time, he wasn't in the room. There were others, other associates of Mr. McCloskey. And that is the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you know who Mr. Bursik is?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know because every time we would meet, those present would be introduced to the people in the room we held our discussions in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, as a result of these discussions and negotiations that you've had with Mr. McCloskey, the end result was a preparation of a statement of facts and acceptance of responsibility which was attached to a motion filed with the Court. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. Don't ask me about the order in which these matters took place. I know that we talked. After that, I decided to acknowledge my guilt. And after that, my lawyer saw to the administrative and legal portion of it. Also, don't ask me about that, I can't actually say. I don't know the legal procedure set in place for that kind of thing. But we did discuss matters. I decided to enter a plea of guilty. Afterwards, my lawyers went around going about the business that they were supposed to do with respect to various agreements and additions, annexes, or whatever they're called. I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, the order is important, Mr. Nikolic, so let's walk it through. The Prosecution filed a motion May 6th, I believe, and then May 7th containing a statement of facts and acceptance of responsibility as Annex A to that document. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sometime thereafter, sometime thereafter, Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Bursik, and perhaps others, came over for a -- not taking a statement, but sort of a question and answer session where they were trying to plug in some holes to what you had already given them in the statement of facts. Do you recall that? I believe I can give you the dates. May 28th, 29th, and 30. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that those were the dates when we had our discussions, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, your discussions were not tape-recorded. That we know as a fact. What we do know also is that we have been provided by the Office of the Prosecution with a transcript of a tape-recorded -- it says: "Conversation between Bruce Bursik and Momir Nikolic." And in this, it's actually Peter McCloskey asking you most of the questions. Do you recall seeing that document with your lawyers?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If, Mr. Karnavas, you're talking about an information report, and Mr. Bursik tendered that, then I have seen that piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just a second, Your Honour. I seem to have misplaced my exhibit list here. We'll do it another way. If we could provide you with P82, what has been marked as P82, if you could just look at that, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that, Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, I do recognise this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is it, please, for the record?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a statement by Momir Nikolic, along with a joint proposal for considering the agreement on a guilty plea between Momir Nikolic and the OTP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, is that the statement of facts that we're talking about, the statement of facts and acceptance of responsibility? Tab A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I wonder whether we have the right document just furnished to us because we got P81. That is annex B or Tab B. We should come to annex A, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I wonder if the witness was provided with the right document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The witness may have been, but I don't know if we have provided you with that, Your Honour. If I may have a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have a statement which is indicated as being Tab B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, there's no problem. My question is whether you have annex A or Tab A.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, I don't have it here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see that, Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it and I recognise this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And this document is the statement of -- contains the statement of facts and acceptance of responsibility we talked about?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I could -- if we could provide you with D33/1, D33/1, take a look at it and let us know whether you recognise that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, now it's time for a break. Would you please furnish the witness with the document and ask him to go over it during the break. Then we come back for your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If it would be convenient, I could furnish him with all the documents for this chapter of my cross-examination, and we can move along. And I apologise for the delays.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You want me to do it on the record, furnish him with all the documents now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may go through the Registrar during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But not during the break or during the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: During the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: During the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And then we will come back and you may ask your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I apologise for the Monday-morning delays.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Blagojevic, please continue. I'm sorry, I'm terribly sorry. Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's okay. That's all right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, during the break, did you have an opportunity to look over some documents? Were any documents presented to you?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. I was given the transcript of the conversation dated the 15th of December, 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If it's okay with you, I would like to go through the documents one by one. If you could -- and we'll get to that one dealing with 1999 with Mr. Ruez. But for the record, and I'm referring now to P82, do you see -- do you have with you what is titled, "Statement of facts and acceptance of responsibility," which was part of the plea agreement?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, I do have that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe that's dated May 6th. That's 2003. Is that correct? It should be right --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then there is D33/1, conversations between Bruce Bursik and Momir Nikolic. Do you have that in front of you? And for the record, that's D33/1. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that has a date of 28 May, 2003, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe -- you've seen this document before, have you not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen it before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think if you would flip to it, flip through it, you need not do it now, but at least on the English version, on 114, page 114, we see the date of 30 May 2003 as part of tape 2, side B. Would it be fair to say that these conversations between you and Mr. McCloskey, though it's titled "Bruce Bursik and Momir Nikolic" took place during the period 28th May, 29th, and 30th May 2003?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, you said page 114, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, in the English version. I apologise. If you would flip through it, the last date of your conversations with Mr. McCloskey and Bruce Bursik were --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, you should have a very brief section of 12 June as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just noticed that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I've found it. I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then I believe if you flip a few pages further down, it notes that you also met again, again with Mr. McCloskey and others, on 12 June 2003. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: In the B/C/S version, it's on page 132.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, for not having that handy.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I've found that, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And it's my understanding, at least from the receipts that we have received from the Prosecution, it was delivered both in English and B/C/S on June 20th, 2003. Would that be more or less your understanding based on your memory of the events?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when I received it, but I know that I received this in the Detention Unit. But I really can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, if you could kindly look at what has been previously marked as D29/1, it's titled "information report." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Information report," yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A report from Mr. Bursik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's correct. And does it not have the date on it of June 23, 2003?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just let me have a look.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's on the very first page, 23/06/2003. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see that, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Now, from our receipts, it appears that the English version was delivered on June 24th, and the B/C/S version would have been prepared and delivered on July 4. That is subsequent to your conversations with Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Bursik back on May 28, 29, 30th, and June 12th. Would it be correct, sir? Do you recall when exactly you received it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly what the date was when I received this, but I think that I saw this document, or rather, I received this document for the first time from my lawyers. They were the ones that gave it to me first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the dates that we have, it would appear that this information report would have been given to you after your conversations with Mr. McCloskey and Bruce Bursik.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what it says here, when it was submitted. According to the dates, it was after the conversation, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then there was one last -- we'll go through all of these. There's another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For the record, we're talking about D30/1. It's proofing notes. This is a letter dated September 16.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you have that, sir? Do you recall seeing that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I have here the English version, I think, and another document attached to it. But I don't think it has anything to do with this particular document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if that is the case, I apologise, and we'll make one available to you right now. Do you have that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do have that. It says: "Report compiled during the proofing session on the 10th, 11th, 12th, 15th, and 16th September 2003."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And if my memory serves me correct, you might have met with the Prosecution after this, but I might be wrong. You know, after receipt of this?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, after this I don't think we met again, although I don't exclude the possibility. But as far as I remember it, I don't think there were any more meetings after this in the Detention Unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's stick with this document, if you will. On page 2 of the English version, and it should be page 2 or page 3 of yours, it indicates that "during the proofing sessions," and I'm referring to, for Madam Usher, on page 2, it says "Re: Information report by investigator Bruce Bursik." So if you could focus your attention on that portion. Do you see that section, sir?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first sentence says: "The witness points out that the report contains a number of mistakes," does it not, sir?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said something to that effect, but not quite that literally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And the information report that we are referring to is the information report that you have in front of you which has been marked for identification purposes D29/1. Are we not talking about that information report?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is Mr. Bursik's report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Those were, for everybody here in the courtroom, those were notes taken by Mr. Bursik during the interviewing sessions that you held with him, the Prosecutor, and your lawyers at the Detention Unit. Those are the ones that were not tape-recorded. Is that not a fact?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it states further down in that same section: "The witness says that there were more mistakes like this," pointing to a mistake referenced earlier. "They were not discussed in the course of this proofing session." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that sentence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And it would appear from reading that sentence that during the proofing session between you and your lawyers, you had some objections as to what the Prosecutor's investigator had written down during your conversations when you all were in the Detention Unit with no tape recorder, and it was just you, the Prosecutor, and your lawyers, and an interpreter, of course. Right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I can tell you exactly what my objections were. After having read these notes by Mr. Bursik in their entirety, and I said during that conversation that there were quite a number of errors in the translation and in the phrasing of sentences that I uttered during the course of the conversations we had over several days. I said that, and I also said that I really am unable to comment on the way in which Mr. Bursik took those notes. They are his notes. I also told Mr. McCloskey that with regard to the notes and the accuracy of those notes, I'm unable to comment, and that I stand by what I said in my statement when my statement was recorded. So that is what we discussed at the time, what I said, and the objections I made. And I wish to say once again to Their Honours that anything that is not clear regarding Mr. Bursik's notes, they are his notes. I don't know how he understood everything that I said because we spoke about countless issues, and this was not in any chronological order. He took notes in writing. And I didn't have occasion to discuss those notes or to have insight into them as this was in English, and what I did read in detail was the report, or rather the information that I received in the Detention Unit. And I really cannot and do not wish to comment on Bursik's notes, nor on the way he wrote them down, how he understood things, what the translation was like, et cetera. These are all things that I cannot comment on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact, in fact, you said as much here under oath when you were being directed by the Prosecutor on Tuesday, 23 September 2003. Isn't that a fact? Let me put it another way. I have a transcript here that was provided to us by the Tribunal. On page 1835, and this was dated -- this was the afternoon session when, Mr. President, you were unavailable. It states here: "I have no further comment to add. I did go through the notes, and I would prefer not to comment on the way that gentleman compiled those notes." And I'm reading from lines 2 to 5. Then you go on. You say: "However, I can confirm here now that my words were accurately recorded and reflected in the transcript." And then later on, you say: "I think there are a number of mistakes there in that transcript because we spoke countless times of certain issues. We went back to the same issues countless times. And I'm really not in a position to comment on everything that's written there. These are the gentleman's notes. That's my opinion. The notes are his, not mine. I said whatever I said exactly in the way in which it is reflected in my statement." And I have just read all the way down to line 13 on page 835. Do you recall making that statement at the conclusion of your direct examination by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember, Mr. Karnavas, that I said what is stated in the transcript, and I didn't say anything other than that now. Nothing different from what I said in that transcript. So I'm unable to quote exactly what I said five days ago, but I said more or less the same thing just now, and I underline once again, Mr. Karnavas, that I cannot comment on Mr. Bursik's notes because they are his notes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, just so I have it straight, the only other people that may be able to comment on Bursik's notes would be, for instance, your lawyers that were there as witnesses. Right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, Mr. Karnavas. I do not know exactly when my lawyers were present. There were moments and days when they were not present, so I can't say when exactly they were present and when they were not present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So just so I have it right, am I to understand, are we to understand that there were times when you were with Mr. Bursik and the Prosecutor when your lawyers were not present?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. My lawyers were there during a part of the preparations. And certain meetings, they were not present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. On May 28th, 29th, 30th, and I believe June 12th, we have you giving a tape-recorded statement. Were your lawyers present then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, just to clarify the record, there were some mistakes on the dates of that tape-recorded statement, and Mr. Bursik fixed those in an addendum that was provided to counsel. And you should have that, or I've got a copy here if you'd like it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, actually, and I appreciate the assistance. God knows I could use all I can up here. But I was referring to actually the May 28th statement, and not the one that was corrected by Mr. Bursik which just coincidentally happened to have the same dates. But I appreciate and I thank the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, getting back to my question, the conversation that you had with Mr. Bursik and Mr. McCloskey subsequent to you changing your plea was tape-recorded, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the part that is in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But when you were meeting with the Prosecution and your team who were there to assist you during the negotiations on the statement of facts, that part was never tape-recorded?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no, it was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at least while you disagree with Mr. Bursik in his information report, would it not be fair to say that at least we have your own lawyers as witnesses as to what you might have said when they were present in the room when you were being -- when you were debriefing or briefing Mr. McCloskey and his team?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the recording of that conversation, my lawyers, as far as I can remember, were always present during the conversations and during the recording of this transcript.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Precisely. And because they were present and because there's no tape-recording, and because now you dispute what Bruce Bursik has written down as far as what you said, it would stand to reason that your lawyers are indeed witnesses to those conversations, are they not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, while they were present at those meetings, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, one of your lawyers obviously speaks Srpski, your language, B/C/S as it's known over here?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other lawyer is an English speaker?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, German and English.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And Mr. McCloskey obviously, and Mr. Bursik, were questioning you in English through a translator. Right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course, your Defence team had their own translator to assist both you and Mr. Londrovic while you were briefing the Prosecutor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it since they were in the room and they heard everything and they were witnesses, that they must have, upon receiving the information report rushed to you, as your Defence lawyer, to point out the numerous errors contained in Bruce Bursik's information report. Did they do that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my lawyers and I discussed the mistakes which appeared in the interpretation of what I had said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Was it them -- assuming that we are correct that the English version was given to them on June 24th, and the B/C/S version was given to you on July 4th, do you recall whether Mr. Londrovic or Mr. Kirsch came to you to point out the errors that Mr. Bursik had made in his information report? Did they come to you and say, "We have this information report, we don't have it in B/C/S yet, but it contains significant errors or numerous errors," however you want to put it? Did they say that? Did that happen?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My lawyers, after we received this information report, discussed with me, and together we agreed that in this information report there were erroneous translations and interpretations. And the three of us discussed this together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, we're a little handicapped today because we don't have any tape-recording that would verify or that would help us out in determining whether you and/or your lawyers are incorrect, or whether it is Mr. Bursik who is incorrect in what exactly was said by you, how it was translated, and then how it was written down on paper?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I really don't see that I can be responsible for something not being recorded. I simply acted in accordance with the lawyers' instructions and as I was told I should do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just for the record, I'm not accusing you of doing anything wrong. But I'm merely making a statement or with an inflection, is that we don't have a tape-recording to at least compare and contrast to see who might be correct, who might be incorrect. We don't have that, do we?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I am describing here what happened, and I am doing so when I have a chance to do that; that is to say, what is true and what is not true. But I must tell you once again that all that I am saying now is something that I discussed with my lawyer, and I have nothing more to add. I did indicate that there were errors. I said that the interpretation of what I said was not correct. My lawyers agreed with me. And here, in this courtroom, I'm presenting this as errors that we identified, that we discussed, and I also told Mr. McCloskey the things that I disagreed with. And I also said that I didn't wish to comment on Mr. Bursik's notes. He probably heard it like that, wrote it down like that, and there's nothing I can do about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And of course Mr. McCloskey heard what Mr. Bursik must have heard and what your lawyers must have heard as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. He's speculating on material that is obvious and irrelevant. I don't know where we're going from this. We were -- I think it's clear what was going on here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll ask another question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you held your proofing sessions on -- at least according to this document, there were several days here. The 10th, the 11th, the 12th, the 15th, and the 16th, was that the first time during those proofing sessions that you brought it to Mr. McCloskey's attention that you strongly or had some feelings, disagreements with Mr. Bursik's recitation of what exactly you had said during those many sessions that you held with him, the Prosecutor, and your lawyers?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I think that that was the first occasion I had to tell Mr. McCloskey because I had no other occasion in view of the date when I received the transcript and when I had the time to read it through and to review it in detail. As far as I can remember, those were the first days that we met after that; that is, Mr. McCloskey, his associates, and myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But of course it was provided to you on July 4th, so you would have had July, August, and half of September to itemise in great detail everything that you took exception with with respect to what Mr. Bursik had written down, for your lawyers to present that to Mr. McCloskey, right? Surely they had access to Mr. McCloskey, and they certainly were meeting with you during that period.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether my lawyers had any contacts with Mr. McCloskey during that period. Possibly they did. I do know that they had contacts with me. I don't think we had any throughout the month of August. And I think that this was the first opportunity when we could seriously discuss these things, that is, in September. I was the only one who had all that time at my disposal, that is, from the moment I received the document up until the time we had occasion to discuss it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Just to pick an example, if we could, and I'm going to refer to page 8. It's in the English version. I don't know exactly what page it would be in the B/C/S, but I'll read the statement that Mr. Bursik attributes to you as having said to him, to your lawyers, to Mr. McCloskey, during those sessions that you were having. It states, page 8, and I'm referring to, for identification purposes, this is D29/1, it says: "Nikolic states that on 12 July" --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I truly apologise.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among all these documents, it's a bit difficult to find my way. What document are you talking about, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the information report from Bruce Bursik. Now, I apologise. I'm getting ahead of myself.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 8. I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know if it's going to be exactly on page 8. But if I could read it, and then maybe you could look for that section, and then we can see whether I've read it correctly. But it states, it starts with: "Nikolic states that on the 12th July, he believes that Mladic, Krstic, and Blagojevic met, as was their norm early each morning during this period. He believes that the three officers discussed the execution making it a pointless exercise for him (Nikolic) to return to Blagojevic that morning to inform him of the execution plan." Have you been able to locate that section, sir?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, this is a statement that claims that you stated that every morning, you would have Mladic, Krstic, and Blagojevic sitting around together having meetings throughout this period.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karnavas. That was not my meaning. I said that in my testimony, too, in connection with the meeting on the 12th because during my testimony, I said that there was some dilemma in my mind as to whether that meeting was held on the 12th or the 13th, was it the 12th and the 13th? And on the basis of insight into a document which I was shown by the Prosecutor, I confirmed that the meeting as stated in that document was indeed held on the 12th in the Bratunac Brigade. And I wish to add the following: After such a long period of time, I really am unable to mention all the meetings and everything I saw in the Bratunac Brigade because from the moment the main staff officers arrived, there were so many of them that it is very difficult to put them in chronological order. As for this meeting every day early in the morning, I said the following, and I explained that. I said that it was customary. If there was a meeting on the 12th, then it was customary for the meetings of commanders to be held early in the morning. And that is what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could I get a question in now?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is unnecessary commenting by the counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, just put your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring to this section, this paragraph. I am not asking you what you testified to or what you believe. I'm asking you to look at what Bruce Bursik said that you said to all those folks in that clandestine atmosphere that all of you were in where nothing was tape-recorded and we have no way of verifying what exactly was said by you or the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Object to the form of the question. He's pointing his finger at the person, he's talking about clandestine, and he's asking the witness a question he has already answered. This is not helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, remember my instruction. I asked you to put a specific question to this witness. But you make a comment there that's not proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, it states here categorically that on the 12th, Mladic, Krstic and Blagojevic met as was their norm. As was their norm. Those three people meeting together. That's what it says here, does it not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, he started it with another statement, "It states categorically." That's a statement, not a question, and it's also an incorrect statement, so again, objection to the form of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll read it again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it not state here that you stated to Mr. Bursik, to the Prosecutor, to your lawyers that on July 12th or 12th July, "he believes that Mladic, Krstic, and Blagojevic met as was their norm early each morning during this period"? Does it not state this in this document?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, what I said exactly I repeated in my statement, the one I gave with respect to this meeting.
