And remember, we are dealing with someone who by profession, being in the intelligence, you know has certain tools of the trade that are used in common day. And I think during our cross-examination today, we learned a little bit about how one goes about making up a story based on part fact and part fiction. So I think we need to tie him down. And also, might I add -- I know he's the Prosecution's witness, but we're dealing with a situation where 7.000, 6.000, 8.000 people were killed. This is the largest massacre, according to the experts, in western Europe since World War II. I believe that this case deserves some time. Also, I would like to point out that Mr. Blagojevic is looking at a life sentence, and this gentleman wishes to enjoy a 20 -- 15- to 20-year sentence. And Your Honours at the end of the day will need to make an assessment as to how truthful this person was because the option is for a life sentence. And just recently, in Indonesia, where a cooperative witness in the Bali incident, with the Prosecutor arguing for 20, the Court stated no, life sentence. And there were 220 victims in that case and here we're talking about, so... And I'm not suggesting what sentence you give him. But what I am saying is you're going to need to make an assessment as to how cooperative he was, and I'm using the language that was prepared by none other Mr. McCloskey, that he cannot fabricate anyone else's involvement. And I think to make a statement that somebody actually killed six people and to bring that into his story in order to benefit because he thinks the Prosecutor needs more information than he already has, and that we have that on the record, I think this is significant. And I'm confident that this individual will come to The Hague, and we can make the necessary arrangements with the Registrar. He can make the necessary arrangements to take a deposition of the gentleman. I can work it either way. But the gentleman is in Bratunac, he's ready, willing, and able, and he has already spoken with the police. And I see no reason why these documents cannot be used to confront Mr. Nikolic. And then subject to connection, the Trial Chamber can make a decision whether this should come in or whether this should be left out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, after consultations with my colleagues, this Bench arrived at the conclusion that we believe the Defence has the right to confront the witness with any documents at their disposal. And since this document arrived before he finished his cross-examination, it is allowed to confront this witness with that document. We hereby order the Registrar to translate those documents in an expeditious manner. And I hope we could get it by tomorrow morning at 9.00. At the same time, we ask Mr. Karnavas, the Defence team of Mr. Blagojevic, to furnish the B/C/S version to the Prosecution and to other parties in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We have, Your Honour, already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The next matter is about the scheduling. Did I hear you that you'll spend the whole day for tomorrow for your cross-examination? Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe you heard me right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm very disappointed about that because in our scheduling ruling the other day, we said that we will give you about 12 to 15 hours for your cross-examination, which is more than that of the Prosecution. And in the last three days, we made an extra effort to sit in the afternoon, which you got 90 minutes more than usual sittings. We hope that you could wind up your cross-examination as soon as possible, maybe in the first session of tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, with the utmost respect, and I know you're disappointed, and I would like to please everybody in the courtroom, but I have a particular mandate, if it will. There's a great deal of areas -- there are many areas that I have yet to go into. Some of them are very quick. May I recall to everyone's attention that the Prosecution did not go over the rules. Obviously, they're entitled to do their direct however they wish. However, I believe that was necessary groundwork in order to lay the foundation for what came thereafter. Now, had the Prosecution decided, and again, it's optional on their part to do that, I might not have spent as much time. And I'm trying to be as efficient as the Court would like. We also have a witness who at times gives lengthy explanations, sometimes unnecessarily. And I'm put in a position where I either have to appear argumentative with the witness and abusive, or sit there like a potted plant, as I have been on many occasions, exercising my breathing technique.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, when we made that ruling the other day, everything goes according to that schedule. We said that we are going to start the next witness on Wednesday and spend two days on that witness. And on Friday, we believed that the Jokic's team also need one day for the preparation for their cross-examination. So everything should go according to the schedule. And Mr. Stojanovic already indicated that they need one sitting, that is, more or less 75 minutes, for their cross-examination to this witness. I believe there's some redirect from the Prosecution. Mr. McCloskey, could you please indicate to me how much time do you need for your redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't really -- I can't think of anything right now, Your Honour. If you have any suggestions, I can help out the Court. But I don't have anything right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you mean that you are not going to redirect this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Not yet, Your Honour. I don't see any point I need to make, though if you need any help on that, I can go into it. But we tried to make it as clear as we could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I'm sure that there's some questions from the Bench because we have some questions concerning certain areas which is not quite clear. We need some clarification from this witness. And that will take some time. And we also have to admit bundles of the documents. And by the way, I believe that the document list you prepared is very good. It's easier to find those particular documents. But anyway, you don't have the whole day tomorrow for your cross-examination, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, if I could use the Prosecutor's time, Your Honour, since they are willing to give it up. Then we should be able to finish tomorrow. I will try, Your Honour. I will try. I'm really working as hard as I can. I really am. But there are certain areas such as this, getting the documents in, that are time-consuming. But let's see how it goes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, how about that you finish your cross-examination by 1.45 tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And we leave some time for the cross-examination by Mr. Jokic's team tomorrow afternoon, 3 to 4.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. Well, it's not fine, but I'll have to live with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You have to say that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We gave you, you know, an extra three sittings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's so decided.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could we have the witness now. Madam Usher. Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm sorry for the late start, because we had some procedural matters to discuss. Now, are you ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am ready, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, during the break, did you have an opportunity to look at the documents that were provided to you?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I could turn your attention to what has been marked as D27/1 for identification purposes, could you please look at it. If I may help, it's the decision. It's a decision by the court, basic court. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have found it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in this decision, it notes that the enterprise formally known as Kartonaza has been changed to SM-PRO Ltd. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If you look at what has been previously marked for identification purposes as D23/1, and it says: "the Basic Court in Bijeljina" at the top. And this talks about the change of ownership.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there's a list -- okay. And this basically demonstrates that it went from a state ownership to a private ownership, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could look at what has been previously marked as D24/1 for identification purposes, that is the document in your language which would designate you as the company manager.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, this is dated 18 October 2000. And at the bottom, it designates that it is a form, attachment 4 to the decision. Does it not say that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Attachment number 4 of the decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the decision that we're talking about is the decision that I first showed you which for identification purposes was D27/1, that decision? You can see it's the same date?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we could say that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Then if we go to D25, what has been previously marked for identification purposes as D25/1, that is the form that has both your signature and your thumbprint or your fingerprint on it. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And is this not, sir, also part of the same package -- the same attachment package to the decision of 18 October 2000?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like to draw your attention to what has been previously marked as D20/1 for identification purposes. Could you please look at it, sir. It's a package of documents, but I'm really interested for the time being on the first one, two -- well, let's look at them all first, and then we'll decide how we'll proceed. Just please look at them.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took a look at it earlier on in the group of documents that you gave me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And the first page of D20/1 is a letter addressed to me, and it's from SM-PRO Bratunac. And in fact, it has a date on it of 15 September 2003, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is a letter here, some kind of letter, with the contents as they're put.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just for the record, let me read it, and then we'll discuss it at some point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We don't have these documents that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm shocked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: D20. Do we have it to be put on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, we could put it on the ELMO, and there must have been a -- I know we're into Monday afternoon now, but... I apologise to the Prosecution. I assumed they had a copy of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now this letter dated September 15th, 2003, states - it's addressed to me - "we are informing you that we have inspected the archives of ODP Kartonaza, currently called SM-PRO, as you requested, and found invoice number 117/2000 issued by d.o.o. 'Amstel' Valjevo, on the basis of which 7,520 KM," that's convertible marks, "were paid out in ready money (cashier's order number 82, dated June 29, 2000), and invoice number 84/2000 dated May 10, 2000, d.o.o. `Meteor' from Valjevo on the basis of which 9,380 KM," convertible marks, "were paid out in ready money (cashier's order number 81, dated June 30, 2000)." And then it has the enclosure. Is that how your copy reads, sir?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, that's how it reads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we could go to the next document that is contained within what has been previously marked as D20/1 for identification purposes, and if you could please look at it, sir. And at the top of it, it says "Enterprise Amstel" on the left side and "ODP Kartonaza" on the right side. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it notes that there's a date, 12 June 2000, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the invoice number is 117/2000. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there is a signature, is there not, on this document, or signatures, are there not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are several signatures, one, two, three, four, in fact. Four signatures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Any of them yours, Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this document, as I understand it, it's a delivery of goods from Amstel to Kartonaza. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we could look at the next document which is contained in D20/1 for identification purposes, top side of it says "cashier's order." And do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the cashier's order. Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dated June 29, 2000. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's invoice number 82. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's for the amount of 7.500, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7.520 KM, convertible marks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And a convertible mark at that time was approximately the same value as a Deutschemark. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Republika Srpska and Bosnia-Herzegovina, that was roughly the exchange rate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is a payment from Kartonaza to Amstel, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it has your signature, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I approved this order for payment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And the payment, in fact, is for cash, right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could now -- if you could look at what has been previously marked for identification purposes as D21/1. I don't know if the Prosecution was given a copy of that. We have an extra copy. And we apologise. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do see that, Mr. Karnavas, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I could read this into the record, this is a letter dated -- well, I believe I don't see the date on it. Or does it have a date? 7 July. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here, Mr. Karnavas, the 7th of July, number 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Okay. But at the bottom, it says -- it's signed September 15, 2003, Amstel Valjevo, and it has director Milena Mitrovic.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, does it not state in this document, sir, that -- well, let me just read it. "In response to your request, we hereby inform you that company Amstel d.o.o. Valjevo did not maintain business relations with ODP Kartonaza Bratunac in year 2000." Does it not state that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it states, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then it states: "Company Amstel d.o.o. Valjevo had 36 invoices in its documentation pursuant to the annual account and for the year 2000 in the period between 01/01/2000 and 12/31/2000. Mention invoice number 117/2000 from June 12, 2000, does not exist in our files, and we know nothing of it." Does it not say that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so it would appear that the invoice 117 to which you paid to Amstel which bears your signature is a false receipt, isn't it? It's a false payment receipt.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is absolutely not correct. Everything here -- you can see everything from this invoice, and I should like to ask you, or rather the Trial Chamber for you to complete what you have to say, and then I should like to ask Their Honours to allow me to explain the details of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Let me ask a few more questions before we get into that. And perhaps before you give your explanation, we can go into the next segment which has to do with Meteor. But while we're still with respect to Amstel, you do not dispute the fact that the receipt itself carries your signature. You recognise that signature? You recognise it to be yours, do you not, sir?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, I am not questioning the fact that I approved this invoice. That means -- and you'll understand this once you hear my explanations and when I explain the situation as it was when I arrived and why I had this kind of relationship. So none of the invoices which came -- fell due for payment in the accounts department of the company where I was director could not have been paid out or anything else done pursuant to it until it was brought to my table for approval. As you can see in both these invoices, or rather on these invoices, you have my approval, my signature stating that I approved the payment pursuant to the invoice. So you have the Amstel invoice, and you have the invoice dated - just a moment, please - the invoice from Valjevo, from Meteor from Valjevo, where I approved in similar fashion the payment pursuant to the invoice that reached our enterprise. And that, Mr. Karnavas, is the -- my discretionary right, how I'm going to act in matters of payment. That is to say, from the account of the company I was director of. Nobody else has the right to make that decision and to approve payments. And you are able to see what my authorisations were, that is to say, they were authorisations without restrictions and limitations, giving me the right to control everything with respect to financial transactions in the company, to approve or not to approve the various payments. Of course, everything must be in keeping with positive legal rules and regulations and the law governing financial undertakings. Now, if I may, I should like to explain to the Trial Chamber before we go on to the next company and the next invoice the following: That the overall situation, what I found when I came to join Kartonaza, and I should like to ask Their Honours to give me the time to answer and explain that. And afterwards, I think things will be much clearer, and my relationship and why I acted in this particular manner and all the rest of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may ask a few questions before you launch into your explanation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object on foundation. If counsel could perhaps -- and relevancy, where this is all going. I think that a business litigation in the former Yugoslavia is probably one of the areas that is more complex than anything to do with what we could think up militarily. And I would object on the grounds that this is more time-consuming than it is probative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, I think there's some sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, Mr. McCloskey here has brought this gentleman in here saying that he's an honest and truthful individual. And here we're showing through these records, he can give whatever explanation he wishes, but the records are fairly clear. And we maintain that this individual has a past where he is less than honest. This is a crime of dishonesty. And it goes to his character. Obviously, it's something that the Trial Chamber will need to consider in evaluating what weight, if any, to give to his testimony. And I think that is why we brought. Now, I can spend two or three days on other material. I have not. I'm limiting it. But I think this is a prime example of where a phony receipt is paid out bearing the gentleman's signature to a company that acknowledges it had no business. And it's interesting to hear his explanation, and then perhaps the Prosecutor can argue that nonetheless the gentleman has a clean past, he's truthful, he's honest, he doesn't have any crimes of dishonesty. And might I also add if you look at the presentencing brief that was prepared by his own lawyers, there's a segment there, there's a segment there that talks about his lack of criminality. So this is important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I understand now where counsel is going. But I would renew my objection in that we have a few documents, many of which are letters to counsel, to try to get to the bottom of this, do we need to get in expert witnesses from the company and how these things work. It goes on endlessly, so I say this is much less probative than it is helpful in getting to the truth of the matter. I just -- in most countries, you must have a criminal conviction of some sort to impeach a witness of something like this. Unless there's something clear and precise we can get to, this is just endless.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that, you know, this set of cross-examination goes to the credibility of this witness. So that's why this Bench allowed the continuation of the cross-examination. But, Mr. Karnavas, could we go through all those as soon as possible since we have -- we have the documents at your hands. We know your point in that cross-examination. You may raise some questions direct to this witness and ask for some explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if we could go back to what has been previously marked as D20/1 for identification purposes, if you could look at that. And now I want to focus your attention on another couple of documents that refer to another company called Meteor, Valjevo. Do you see them, sir?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in essence again, these two documents demonstrate that a cashier order, cash, was signed over by you to Meteor based on an invoice, number 81. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The invoice number is 80 -- there's a mistake here. It is 84 as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. There's one 84, and what is that for, the 84/2000? What are we looking at?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are looking at an invoice, and the contents of that include general repair of Sloter and two Krajsers, repair of a Pivano cutting device, and purchase of new cutting devices for the machines that were repaired. So we have an invoice for items linked to the repair of one of the Kartonaza plants. And the machine is actually called Kartonaza in this enterprise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then we have a cashier's order with -- bearing again your signature, does it not, for I believe it's 9.380 KM, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, would it be surprising to you if I were to tell you that Meteor is a company for trade; it is not licensed or capable of repairing printing machinery? Would that surprise you?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would not surprise me because the Meteor company is a company, to the best of my knowledge, undertakes supplies for tools and everything else necessary for the repair of heavy machinery. And pursuant to a demand from us, this company procured everything we required in order to perform a general repair of Kartonaza. That is to say, Sloters, Krajsers, and all the other devices that were the subject, the Pivano cutting device which is an Italian-produced knife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if the Court were to issue a subpoena to get the records, the payment records, would it surprise you that there's no such payment to Meteor in their giro account for these services that they allegedly provided for which you paid for and signed? Would that surprise you?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, as far as payment and the payment records, that's where you have the problem. As regards the recording and payment recording, everything was possible in the former Yugoslavia. So it was possible for you to come to a company which you have been doing business with for ten years, and not to find a single invoice. Or on the other hand, they might issue a certificate saying that they never recorded any payments in their company. And I wish to say before this Tribunal this was the only method in which money could be paid out because it was business transactions with Serbia at the time, and there were no payment transactions with Serbia at that time. So there was no other way in which payment could be made except in cash, ready money, which means that in accounting department, Mr. Karnavas - and quite obviously you haven't been informed about these issues - they're not able to record convertible marks there because there's not allowed to do so. It would be an offence. So they couldn't do that. So I wouldn't be at all surprised if they were to come here and tell us that they have nothing in our accounts department if they said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's precisely --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, we are not litigating on commercial transactions. You have to understand, if you have some verdict made by a court or judgement rendered by a tribunal, you may show it to us. I think that's the easiest way to prove your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. If I may ask one last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, if you think it's proper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you acknowledge to creating invoices that don't properly reflect what they claim to reflect. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can't put it that way, Mr. Karnavas, and ask for a yes or no answer. First of all, you're claiming something that does not stand, that is not correct. I don't create the invoices. It is services that are being invoiced, so I didn't create the invoices. The invoices came from companies who sent me the goods or performed services. So it's not me that draws up the invoices. It is them. And as the person in authority, as the director, I approve the money, payments in the sole way possible at the time, the only method that was used between Republic of Serbia and the Republika Srpska. That was the only way in which payments could be made, that is by cash. Because there were no payment transactions, you could pay nothing through a bank or bank account. And if something doesn't work, if the system isn't in existence, then you couldn't do it. So that's the only reason why we did it this way. And I'd like to ask you, Mr. Karnavas, if you have a single piece of evidence that after this any lawsuits were brought against me or criminal files made because of this, and that I was prosecuted for anything of this kind, please tell me. I have no knowledge of it, and I know that nobody ever raised any questions with respect to the methods of -- the payments functioned in my company. And I also wish to say before this Trial Chamber that you were well able to see -- you could go to the control organ of Republika Srpska, the financial police, and see what the state of affairs was after two controls in a state enterprise such as Kartonaza and the day I left Kartonaza, so before and after, you can look at that. I invited the financial police before I left Kartonaza to look through all the books, of all the financial transactions and to report to the shareholders' meeting, because there were five owners in the end instead of one. We heard a man named Mirko from Zvornik of the financial police, I don't know what his surname was. But you can contact the financial police. They can show you their report. And you will see that on the day I left the Kartonaza company, we had not overstepped our authority anywhere with respect to payments and financial transactions. Everything was in order. And I wish to state one more thing. What you said does absolutely not stand. I was not thrown out of Kartonaza. They offered me the post of technical managing director which I turned down because there was a student that they brought in to sell out the state-owned enterprise Kartonaza, to let the workers go, and then to dispose of everything. So I didn't accept this concept and them bringing in this kind of man. So that's where the conflict lay. When they suggested they let go half the workers, 50 per cent of the workers, I told the workers before I left Kartonaza that if they were sacked, I would be the first to leave if they were sacked. And once I left, I would no longer be able to decide on their fate. Now once I left, after my departure, 95 per cent of the businesses that worked with Kartonaza ceased to do so. All the machinery was sold. All the repair work of the machinery that I had conducted and all the workers were let go. They were all sacked except for two workers. And the situation in the Kartonaza factory was this: There were no more workers and no more machinery to work with. And you can also go to the accounts department, the department that gave you these documents -- just let me finish, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, we're talking about whether you embezzled money or not, that's what this is all about. Not whether they sacked other workers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I think the witness is finishing his testimony. Be a little more patient.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm just about finished, Mr. President, Your Honours. So after I left that company virtually no longer exists. There are only one or two people still employed. All the others have been fired. The entire plant that I overhauled has been sold for next to nothing, for peanuts. Some space is being rented out for a monthly rate. And the plant is a completely new plant. I would like Your Honours to know this, too: When I arrived, nothing was working there. The printing press was at a level of 45 years ago. And I can explain each and every detail. So I claim that this is no forgery of any invoices, no embezzlement, I claim that legally and within my legal competencies, I carried out and approved payments, and I also claim that I approved the payment of money and I didn't take it myself personally. And in the corner, you have the cashier, the signature of the person who received the money on one of these invoices. So I just approved it. You have the person who received the money. One person was the manager of the printing press, and the other person who received the other sum of money was the manager of Kartonaza. So I didn't take the money. I didn't receive it. They pick it up from the cashier. And they gave it to the people who were working in those two companies. That is the whole truth. As for this letter from Serbia, Mr. Karnavas, it doesn't mean anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll move on, Your Honour. I could go into this area, but I think we better move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to talk to you, Mr. Nikolic, about your role as a coordinator. As I understand it from your testimony, your statements, you were tasked on the morning of the 12th by Popovic, Kosoric to locate certain areas where they could store and detain prisoners. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that we discussed this issue, and that I proposed to Popovic and Kosoric facilities where the separated men from Potocari could be temporarily detained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then slightly thereafter, you're given an order by Colonel Jankovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're outside the Fontana, Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The conversation doesn't last more than a few minutes?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he tells you, Captain Nikolic, to go to Potocari to coordinate the various units. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Roughly so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You were a reserve -- in the reserves. You weren't an officer from the military academy; your rank was as a reserve officer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, how long had you been a captain?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. It says in my booklet for how long, but I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you start out as a captain when you joined the Territorial Defence back in 1986?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I had the rank of captain then, but I'm not sure. I'm really not sure. I think that I already had the rank of captain then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, is that a rank that you had earned or was it bestowed upon you when you got the job? All right, let me back up. Before going to the Territorial Defence in 1986, you were a schoolteacher or professor, as you would put it in Bosnia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was a teacher of defence and protection in school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You had attended the military, but you weren't selected or chosen to attend the school for reserve officers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. We have been over this. If there's some foundation counsel makes why we need to go over this again, but time is valuable and I know we have gone over this. And these questions have been asked. And unless we can point to some relevance, I wish we could go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, I think we are discussing the coordination rule by this witness during that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, if I ask a compound question, Your Honour, I've got the Prosecutor there jumping up and down saying I'm trying to confuse the witness. If I break it down, I've got the Prosecutor jumping up and down saying we're going over old territory. So the question I want to ask basically is: Here's a guy from 1986, he's a captain. Now it's 1995. He was a member of the war presidency. He was acting commander of the Territorial Defence. He's not even -- he never attended any academies. He's a reservist. He's not even a first captain, let alone a major. How is it that given his background, his pedigree, how is it that he was still a captain? That's the basis of my question. Now, if I ask it in that form, which is my normal trait, I'm going to get objected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think you have already asked this question, and I think the witness answered: "I think I had the rank of captain then, in 1986."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But my question is how is it nine years later, he's still a captain? And I can't ask all of that unless I kind of lead up to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Why are you still captain in July of 1995 is a perfectly fine question. I wish you would ask it. Or maybe just refer to Boering's questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were still a captain back in 1995 in July. Right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even though at one point you had been the acting commander of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, which failed, and that system no longer existed. It wasn't functioning any longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you had this two -- this short conversation, I don't know how many minutes it took, but maybe you could tell us, this short conversation with Mr. Jankovic, how long did it take?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that it was very brief, some 10 minutes or so. I'm really unable to tell you more precisely than that. It was very brief, the amount of time it took for him to convey to me the order as to what I should do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were alone when this conversation took place? Nobody was there? Nobody was close enough to hear what Jankovic had tasked you, right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He called me. I approached him. And then we spoke alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you've indicated that when you got to Potocari, you found the various units that had been there.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact, at one point, you list them.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, one of them was the 65th Protection Regiment?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I said in my testimony that it was a part of the 65th Protection Regiment. I think that I was referring to the military police because a part of the 65th Protection Regiment were people I knew personally, both officers and soldiers. But I knew most of the officers at least by sight, not by name or positions. But I knew them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, before we go on, do you recall giving a statement to Mr. Ruez back in 15 December 1999?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember talking to Mr. Ruez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember him asking you if the 65th Protection Regiment rings a bell? In fact, I believe it was Peter McCloskey asking you that question. Do you recall Peter McCloskey asking you that question, if the 65th Protection Regiment rings a bell?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, possibly he asked me that. But really I don't remember many details of the questions put to me then in 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you like to have your memory refreshed, or should I just give your answer and see whether that rings a bell?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can do that. It's up to you. You choose which you want to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Question: "Does 65th Protection Regiment ring a bell?" That's McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: May we have reference to the page --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, I stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's page 27, line 23. And in the B/C/S version, it's page 24, line 19. Page 24 in B/C/S, and I believe it's around line 19, somewhere in that neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall being asked the question: "Does 65th Protection Regiment ring a bell?" And you answered: "No, I really don't know. Protection Regiment of the main staff, yes. But the numbering, I didn't read anywhere, I think." Do you recall giving that answer?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, Mr. Karnavas, if that is what it says, then that was my answer. No, really, I don't know. The Protection Regiment, yes, the Protection Regiment of the main staff. But as for numbers, since the end of the war up until the time of this interview, I absolutely had no contacts with the army. It simply didn't interest me. And I forgot whether it was called the 65th or the 95th. It didn't mean anything to me then. So I didn't concern myself with numbers. I said I knew which unit it was then, too. As for the numbers, they really didn't mean anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so I'm clear, four years -- you leave the army in 1996. Is that correct? 1996?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in April. I think it was the 20th of April, 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here we are December 15th, 1999, according to the statement on the first page. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your testimony today is that in three years' time, you simply could not remember the number of the Protection Regiment. That is your testimony today. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying that at the time when I was giving this interview, prior to that, I had no contact, nor did I have any document or anything which would remind me of the units and the numbers of any units. So at the time I was not prepared to talk about numbers because I simply from the day I was demobilised until I was called for the interview, I did not concern myself with these things. And that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Who was the -- who was in charge of the 65th Protection Regiment on July 12th, 1995, when you went to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that I knew the senior officers by sight, and that I know the commander in person. It was first Colonel Savcic, and then Zoran Malinic. He was either a major or a lieutenant-colonel. I'm not quite sure of his rank now. But I did know members of the 65th regiment from the police who were present for a time in Bratunac. I knew them by sight, and I knew which unit they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask the question again, and I'll read it from the screen: "Who was in charge of the 65th Protection Regiment on July 12th, 1995, when you went to Potocari?" Now, that is in Potocari, who was in charge that you dealt with? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I don't know who was the commander of the Protection Regiment in 1995. I don't know. It was a unit of the main staff. I don't know who was appointed to that position. And in my statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Nonresponsive, Your Honour. Nonresponsive. I asked the question for the second time. I asked him -- this is critical to my defence. He indicated that as a captain he went there to coordinate. He's coordinating people a lot higher than him from different units. Now, if he doesn't know, he should say I don't know. But to go on and give a nonresponsive response gets us nowhere, and it's eating the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, the first sentence of his answer to your question, he said, "I don't know who was commander of the Protection Regiment in 1995."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. My question was very narrow. Who was in charge in Potocari on July 12th, because he indicated that the whole regiment wasn't there, a unit was there. So somebody had to be in charge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So you are asking about who is the commander of part of the regiment on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That was in Potocari that he had to deal with and coordinate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who it was?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who it was. Who was the commander of that part of the Protection Regiment that was in Potocari, I don't know his first and last name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his rank?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know his rank. I know him by sight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he -- did you know him personally or did you just know him by sight?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just told you that I knew those men from those units by sight. I don't know them personally. I would see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the person that you were supposed to coordinate from the 65th regiment, unit that was there, you did not know that person, and he -- I guess, axiomatically, that he did not know you at least in a personal sense.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my statement, I didn't say that I went there specifically to coordinate the work in the way in which you are putting it. I was in the role of coordinator, and I said with whom I had direct and personal contact among the officers in charge. I said who I had contact with, and I never mentioned the name of any officer from the Protection Regiment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, you've testified that you were given a mandate by a colonel from the main staff. Right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that mandate required you to coordinate all of the various units, you, a captain, all the various units in Potocari on that morning of 12 July 1995. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My assignment, Mr. Karnavas, was to coordinate the work of units who had been tasked, who knew what they were supposed to do in Potocari. And my task was to supervise them, to solve problems should they arise in this overall operation. So the units that were in Potocari had already received assignments from their commanders, from their superiors. I had no need to know all the commanding officers. My task was to supervise things, to tour the places of engagement. If there are any problems, to suggest and propose solutions to those problems. Those were my tasks as coordinator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The 65th regiment belongs to the main staff, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a unit of the main staff of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's under Mladic, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could say that, though it is within the framework of the security administration in the professional sense. But it is directly subordinated probably to General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you were there to coordinate and give instructions, obviously you would need to have some physical contact and speak with the various units that were there. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas, that what I said. I spoke to the commander because I saw that there were problems. So I spoke to that commander. I mentioned Jevic that I spoke to because there was a problem with respect to the buses, the movement, the transportation. I also spoke to other officers who encountered problems during the operation. For instance, in the town of Bratunac, those buses were stoned at one stage. I got in my car, I went to Bratunac, I found the military police of the Bratunac Brigade, one or two patrols, as many as it was possible to find. I engaged those men, so I then directly ordered the police of the Bratunac Brigade to secure passage through the town because at a certain point in time, that was the main problem. Had a problem arisen somewhere else, I would have gone there, too, to see what the problem was, try and find a way to deal with it. However, in other segments, there were no problems that the officers on the spot were not able to deal with. So that was my role in the simplest terms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Focus with me, we're back in Potocari. It's sometime around noon or 1.00 or 2.00, whenever you get there, on June -- July 12th, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before going there, you had this 10-minute conversation with Jankovic. Did he explain to you exactly how each and every unit was tasked? Did he give you specific instructions and tell you the 10th Sabotage from the main staff has been given this task, 85th this task, MUP this task? Did he do that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I know it's getting late, but there's no such thing as the 85th, so if we could try to keep the facts straight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 65th. 65th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you exactly what each unit was supposed to do? And I'm not asking for an explanation that he told you that they know what they're supposed to do. I'm asking you did he tell you what each unit was tasked to do? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't tell me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the sense that you have put it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well -- so in other words, he didn't tell you what the 65th Regiment was tasked to do, and if so, who tasked them, right?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, he didn't tell me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He didn't you who was in charge of the 65th Protection Regiment at that time so you could make contact with that person, did he?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't tell me who was in charge of the 65th Protection Regiment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Incidentally, did he give you like a letter of recommendation or a letter of introduction so you could introduce yourself as Captain Nikolic when you would be going up to these lieutenant-colonels or colonels or majors, whoever you were coordinating with, to let them know that you had a mandate from none other than the main staff, Colonel Jankovic? Did he give you a letter of introduction?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karnavas. All I can tell you is that most of those officers knew Captain Nikolic, even before they came to Potocari, both from within police ranks and the ranks of these units. I think that many people knew me personally or by sight. They knew who Captain Nikolic was. And I didn't receive any letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, it's time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I thought we were going until 5.00, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, we never did that. Usually we go from 3.00 to 4.30, because the tape will not run two hours. We have to break here. It's very late.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I do wish to point out, though, that we have a little bit of what we call back home filibustering, it's a technique used in the senate, when they don't want to pass the bill, they read the phone book in order to run out the time. And I'm concerned a little bit. So with all due respect, I will need some permission to cut the witness off, or I would request the President to cut the witness off when he's not responsive to direct questions. Because I think we wasted 15 minutes on one question to which finally I got the answer which was no. With that, Your Honour, I mean, it's a little frustrating up here. Maybe that's the game plan, frustrate and evade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no, no, I think as always you have to think the other side as bona fide. And Mr. Karnavas, also on your part, I think there's still room for improvement. You ask the same question once again. And sometimes you are not so direct and to the point. I believe that you have a point to make in those questions, but you could directly come to that question. Because in the cross-examination, you are allowed somehow to ask leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There's always room for improvement, Your Honour. And I agree, and I will -- I certainly will make greater efforts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. And we'll resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning in the same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 30th day of September, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
